verified_observations: memory._atomic_rewrite_jsonl writes backlog JSONL to a unique sibling NamedTemporaryFile and then calls os.replace(tmp_path, path), but performs no explicit flush+os.fsync on that temporary file and no explicit parent-directory fsync inside that helper.

LifeMemory.open(root) and ProjectMemory.open(...) construct Backlog(root / 'backlog.jsonl'). Manager front_door._life_dir_for(mem) resolves the same per-project project_root/project.root/root used for Manager state; daemon._continuous_config_path(life_dir) is life_dir / 'continuous.json'. Thus the normal project-scoped backlog and continuous config share the same parent directory.
daemon._atomic_write_bytes, used by continuous-state persistence, writes the temporary file, flushes it, calls os.fsync(file_fd), replaces the target, and then fsyncs path.parent.

manager_continuous_handoff uses compare_and_swap_continuous_config(..., before_write=_commit). The continuous writer executes its before-replace callback before os.replace of continuous.json, so mission/Manager commit work is ordered before the final continuous-state replace in this path.

Linux fsync documentation distinguishes persistence of file data from persistence of a containing directory entry: fsync(file) does not necessarily persist the directory entry, for which fsync(directory) is needed.

scope_correction.confirmed_gap: The authoritative backlog rewrite does not explicitly fsync the new backlog file's data before it is renamed and before the later continuous-state commit is allowed to become durable. Atomic visibility via os.replace is not by itself proof of power-loss durability of the new file contents.
scope_correction.narrowed_claim: A separate backlog-parent-directory fsync is not independently required by the observed same-directory handoff ordering if the later successful continuous.json commit fsyncs that same parent directory after the backlog rename. That later directory fsync can provide the directory-entry metadata barrier for both renames. The clear source-level asymmetry is therefore the missing backlog file-data fsync, not necessarily a missing second directory fsync.
scope_correction.not_established: No power-loss/crash-injection test was run. Actual persistence behavior is filesystem/OS/storage dependent, and the proposed creation_stamp, exact-insert API, handoff fence, protected_route_fingerprint_v4 and unified reconcile_or_rearm are adaptation proposals rather than implemented or benchmarked Argus behavior.

external_reference.relevance: fsync persists file data/metadata; containing directory entry requires directory fsync

unresolved: Direct power-loss or fault-injection reproduction across the backlog-insert -> continuous-enable boundary.
Whether globally hardening every JSONL rewrite has unacceptable latency/throughput cost versus a narrow durable exact-insert writer.

The worker's proposed creation stamp, v4 route fingerprint, handoff fence and exact-retry regression matrix remain unimplemented designs, so this audit does not attribute measured reliability gains to them.
